$comment: SINGLE declaration of what a self-hosted runner must provide for csq's CI.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Before it, the requirement lived implicitly in nine
separate `ensure-apt-deps.sh` call sites plus an unwritten assumption that
`claude` was on PATH. Nothing stated the whole set, so nothing could check
it, so a runner that lacked half of it was indistinguishable from a healthy
one until a job failed 40 minutes in with a misleading message.
Measured 2026-09-01: the org pool holds two disjoint Linux fleets that both
answer to [self-hosted, Linux, X64]. The `ci-portable` fleet (16) satisfies
these profiles; the `kailash-release` fleet (4) satisfies none of them. Jobs
are label-pinned to `ci-portable` — this file is the belt to that braces: it
catches a runner that carries the label without the capability.
Edit THIS file, never the assert script's internals.

claude-cli.why: Jobs whose tests shell out to the `claude` binary. Its absence is silent: the eval harness records `skipped_cli_missing` and asserts on empty output, and csq-core's phase2b tests fail with `claude binary not found on PATH`. Both read as flakes.

tauri-linux.why: Desktop bundle build (release.yml build-desktop, edition-seam enterprise-build).

harness-sandbox.why: coc-harness runs the eval harness under bubblewrap.

windows-cross.why: cfg(windows) clippy via the mingw cross target.
